Hegseth ligt onder vuur na de door de Republikeinen verloren tussentijdse verkiezingen van vorige week. Onder zijn leiding begonnen de Verenigde Staten een oorlog tegen Iran. Het Republikeinse Congreslid Thomas Massie had het initiatief genomen tot het starten van een afzettingsprocedure en werd daarbij gesteund door de Democraten. Hij stelde dat de oorlog tegen Iran en het gevangennemen van de Venezolaanse leider Nicolás Maduro niet zonder toestemming van het Congres uitgevoerd hadden mogen worden. Maar het voorstel van Massie strandde. De Republikeinen behaalden een meerderheid in het huis met 211 tegen 204 stemmen. The diplomat said Iran was studying proposals on its nuclear activities presented by Qatar, the main mediator. US President Donald Trump spoke by phone with Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani about efforts to de-escalate the conflict and secure a comprehensive agreement, the emir’s office said on Friday. Qatari officials have been shuttling between Doha and Tehran to help bridge differences, including over Iran’s nuclear activities and the US naval blockade of Iranian ports.

items.title: Major losses could spur Trump to escalate war before year's end
items.summary: As much as the Iran war is the key reason Trump and the GOP were crushed tonight, it is important to recognize that the pressure for war is now likely to increase . This does not mean that Trump will restart the war. But the balance of pressure for and against war will likely favor escalation. Trump was under a degree of pressure to strike a deal before the midterms, hoping to soften the blow in the polls. But now that the midterms are over, that pressure will dissipate somewhat. Gas prices are still high, but the political cost has already been paid. There won’t be another point on the political calendar for some time when that cost can be exacted again. But two other factors will intensify. First, pro-war elements in Israel and in Washington will see the next two months as the last period in which Trump has wide maneuverability to restart the war. By January, the Democrats will control both chambers, will control the purse, and can begin impeaching Trump’s secretaries, including Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth. items.title: Aipac spent $55m on losing congressional candidates in midterm elections: Report
items.summary: Aipac spent $55m on losing congressional candidates in midterm elections: Report The American Israel Public Affairs Committee (Aipac) spent more than $84m in the 2026 US midterms, but nearly two-thirds of those funds were spent on losing candidates, according to a new report from Responsible Statecraft. Aipac’s Super Pac and other groups spent $55m on failed candidates. The largest portion of those funds, about $32m, was spent trying to defeat Democratic Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan. The results marked one of Aipac’s worst performances in years, suggesting that the US-Israeli war on Iran, which has contributed to soaring cost-of-living issues, resonated strongly with voters. In the 2022 midterms, Aipac’s Super Pac, United Democracy Project, saw 69 percent of its expenditure spent on races backed by the organisation that won. That number was even higher in 2024, after Israel’s genocide in Gaza, with 87 percent of its spending going to successful races. The group was an early supporter of the war and a major funder of ads attacking House and Senate candidates calling to cut off aid to Israel. It spent big on the 2026 midterm elections, dumping $84.1 million via its super PAC, United Democracy Project (UDP), and several other PACs into races that have been decided as of this writing. AIPAC might be silent today because they need to explain to their donors how nearly-two-thirds, or $55.3 million, of that spending went to races in which the group’s preferred candidate lost. But lost in the conversation is that this was not just a rejection of the Iran war. It was also a repudiation of the broader foreign policy that repeatedly gets the U.S. into wars — or into supporting the wars and war crimes of U.S. partners. In many contests on Tuesday, the U.S.-Israel relationship was on the ballot too, and it was rejected by Republicans and Democrats alike in favor of recentering priorities back to national interests, including ending the flow of military aid to Israel. Trump famously ran on a promise to end forever wars and not to start new ones. clusters.headline: Are Democrats ready to make the most of the blue wave?

items.title: Are Democrats ready to make the most of the blue wave?
items.summary: Unless you’ve been living under a rock (no shame Patrick Star!), you’ve likely heard about last Tuesday’s “Blue Wave” midterm elections . The Democrats’ strong performance at the polls flipped control of the House and the Senate, delivering stunning results on the way, including flipping long-time red states like Kansas and Texas. As the GOP scrambles to repair the damage and Democrats strategize about how to use their new power in a divided Washington, one takeaway seems obvious: this was a foreign policy election, in which the Iran war and the costs it brought home served as the tipping point. But can we read these election results as a repudiation of U.S. foreign policy writ-large, or is this a specific response to one of the dumbest interventions in the long history of American adventurism? What does JD Vance's day-after effort to distance himself from the war tell us about how Republicans are digesting this result? items.summary: After Democrats dominated last week’s midterm elections, retaking control of the House and Senate, President Donald Trump has turned his attention southward. “Cuba is falling. It’s a failing nation. It’s got an ideology very similar to what the Democrat ideology is,” he said Monday. “I would imagine it will fall fairly soon.” The comments suggest that, despite facing a stunning rebuke of his foreign-policy adventurism in Iran, Trump is not quite ready to give up on his goal, reiterated as recently as last month, of overthrowing the Cuban government. So is Trump poised to go beyond economic pressure and saber rattling by launching a military campaign against Cuba? The answer is “no” — or at least “not yet.” Many analysts predict that a lame-duck president constrained by domestic setbacks could seek redemption through foreign-policy achievements, including by lashing out at seemingly easier targets like an impoverished Caribbean nation. At his weekly briefing, the ministry’s media and communications director, Ibrahim bin Sultan al-Hashmi, said mediation was continuing. clusters.headline: How water, energy, and climate are reshaping international security

items.title: How water, energy, and climate are reshaping international security
items.summary: Water, energy, and mineral resources have long played a role in influencing and inciting political, ideological, and economic violence. clusters.headline: 'Junk history' and Swedish neutrality

items.title: 'Junk history' and Swedish neutrality
items.summary: The historian Stephen Kotkin of Stanford’s Hoover Institution has penned an important new essay on the phenomenon of “junk history”: reductionist or plainly wrong interpretations of historical events that have little or no basis in empirical reality but are nevertheless “marshaled in policy debates as justification for action, up to launching wars.” The emblematic example, which has recently been used by advocates for the war with Iran, is the failure of British Prime Minister Neville Chamberlain to truly ensure “peace in our time” at Munich in 1938. As Kotkin once put it, “It turns out not everything is Munich. It turns out Munich wasn’t even Munich when you get down into the nitty-gritty details.” Another example of junk history is what many otherwise well-informed American observers think they know about Sweden’s conduct during World War II and the Cold War. From Rulemaker to Rulebreaker? The 2011 NSG Revision to the U.S.-Saudi Nuclear Deal
Arms Control Now Blog
[email protected] Mon, 11/09/2026 - 15:40

For several decades, the United States and other advanced nuclear states have worked cooperatively to prevent the spread of nuclear weapons and the technologies and materials that can be used to produce them. In the years since, every U.S. president on both sides of the aisle have tried to advance those efforts. In alignment with these efforts, in 2011, the United States spearheaded an international effort to tighten restrictions on the transfer of sensitive nuclear technology that can be used to build nuclear weapons, helping strengthen a nonproliferation norm.

items.summary: As part of an effort to keep Russia on the radar of African countries still struggling from some of the negative externalities of Russia’s continuing war in Ukraine, Russian President Vladimir Putin hosted African leaders in Moscow last week for the third Russia-Africa summit . Between October 28 and 29, Russian officials met with their African counterparts in high-level discussions covering a wide range of issues, primarily focused on continued security relations and opportunities for greater economic collaboration. Of course, Russian engagement with Africa isn’t new. The Russian paramilitary group Africa Corps has around 2,500 fighters on the continent, where it has formed relations with a number of African governments to fight armed groups in exchange for payment, including through access to commodities. items.title: A Fox Under a Pink Moon review – Iranian teen refugee paints boldly imaginative self-portrait

Fleeing a dead-end life as a Tehran maid, Soraya – who is just 16 at the beginning of the film – starts out at an Istanbul asylum centre. Most “games” – as border-crossing sorties with people-smugglers are euphemistically called – end in failure in the wilderness at the hands of hostile law enforcement officers. Soraya is hoping to join her mother, who left for Austria after the death of Soraya’s father when she was a child. She winds up back in the Iranian capital, with her violent husband. La de Amira comenzó cuando todavía era un pequeño corazón latiendo en el interior de su madre y los médicos descubrieron que algo no iba bien. El suyo latía demasiado despacio. Una bradicardia severa -frecuencia cardíaca muy baja- amenazaba con detener el reloj antes incluso de que la vida hubiera comenzado.Hoy Amira tiene ocho meses. Está viva. Y lleva dentro un dispositivo de apenas dos centímetros, el marcapasos más pequeño del mundo, diseñado específicamente para que un corazón tan diminuto como el suyo pueda seguir latiendo. Detrás de esos dos centímetros de tecnología hay meses de trabajo, una doctora que decidió llamar a una puerta que parecía demasiado grande para escucharla, doce ingenieros trabajando contra el reloj, y un científico de 65 años que decidió aplazar su jubilación para intentar salvar a una niña a la que no conocía.Es también, sobre todo, una historia de encuentros. items.title: Corporate Re-entry as an Indicator of the End of the “Age of Wars”
items.summary: Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 marked not only a military but also an economic turning point in the international order. The mass withdrawal of multinational corporations (MNCs) from Russia demonstrated that geopolitical risk had begun to outweigh the benefits of global economic interdependence. But if corporate exit is one indicator of the beginning of a new “age of wars”, the gradual return of MNCs could be an indicator of its eventual end. Corporate return should not, however, be measured as a binary variable of returned/not returned. It is better understood as a sequence of increasingly costly and difficult-to-reverse commitments. This paper proposes a “corporate re-entry ladder” ranging from renewed institutional contacts and market reconnaissance to direct commercial presence and, ultimately, irreversible capital investment. clusters.headline: Centcom sets up 'Task Force Iron Gate' to disrupt Iran’s weapons transfers

items.title: Centcom sets up 'Task Force Iron Gate' to disrupt Iran’s weapons transfers
items.summary: Centcom sets up 'Task Force Iron Gate' to disrupt Iran’s weapons transfers The United States Central Command (Centcom) has directed the establishment of a task force that will support US government's efforts to prevent Iran from using ground routes to transport advanced weapons and other materials. In a statement issued on Saturday on X, Centcom said Admiral Brad Cooper has directed the formation of Task Force Iron Gate, an internal staff of approximately 20 civilian and military personnel based in Tampa, Florida. It will coordinate with other US government agencies on preventing the movement of advanced weapons systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials, and "illegal revenue streams" across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea, Centcom added. "The establishment of Task Force Iron Gate reinforces the success of our ironclad blockade against Iran at sea," said Cooper. "Strengthening CENTCOM's collaboration with U.S. inter-agency partners will further constrain Iran's ability to finance terrorism, rebuild weapons factories, and replenish their military." https://t.co/xUcO5

clusters.headline: IRGC spokesman announces lifting of restrictions on Iranian missiles

items.title: IRGC spokesman announces lifting of restrictions on Iranian missiles
items.summary: IRGC spokesman announces lifting of restrictions on Iranian missiles Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards has said that it has lifted restrictions on the range of Iran's missiles. IRGC spokesman, Brigadier General Hossein Mohebbi reportedly made the comments at a press conference on Saturday, in response to question regarding the country's supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei's warning to the US against further attacks on the country. Khamenei had previously said during a meeting with senior military commanders, that any renewed US or Israeli attck would be met with "with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response". The leader also reportedly ordered an update of Iran's military target database. According to Tasnim news agency, Mohebbi was asked on Saturday whether Khamenei's comments meant that limits on the range of Iranian missiles had been removed. He responded : "This restriction has been lifted for us". “Our duty is to show our capabilities on the battlefield,” he added.

clusters.headline: Voormalig Midden-Oostencorrespondent Thomas Loudon (56) overleden

items.title: Voormalig Midden-Oostencorrespondent Thomas Loudon (56) overleden
items.summary: Journalist en oud-correspondent Thomas Loudon is overleden. Hij kampte met neuro-endocriene tumoren (NET), een langzaam groeiende vorm van kanker. Vorig jaar kreeg hij de diagnose en deze week overleed hij daaraan. Hij was 56 jaar. In 2001 werd Loudon de eerste Nederlandse (video)journalist die zich na de Islamitische Revolutie in Iran vestigde. Hij deed in diverse talen verslag van ontwikkelingen in Iran, Afghanistan en het noorden van Irak voor onder meer de NOS, Trouw en Elsevier, maar ook voor buitenlandse media als CNN, het Chileense Canal 13 en Asia TV in Singapore. Egypte en Jordanië In 2003 trok hij naar de Egyptische hoofdstad Caïro, waar hij Midden-Oostencorrespondent werd voor de NOS. Daarna deed hij dat vanuit Jordanië. Hij maakte onder meer verhalen over de Amerikaanse oorlog in Irak. Correspondent bleef hij tot begin 2007, waarna hij terugkeerde naar Nederland. In de jaren daarna was hij actief als docent journalistiek in Groningen en Rotterdam. Ook richtte hij zijn eigen organisatie op om journalisten te ondersteunen in landen waar de persvrijheid onder druk staat. Daa

items.title: Freezer meltdowns and airline hoaxes are a taste of things to come. Hoping for the best is no longer an option | Elisabeth Braw
items.summary: Acts of greyzone aggression aim to spread panic. Europe has to show the saboteurs that we are resilient It was as though a ghostly hand had switched the settings on supermarket freezers across Europe from “freeze” to “defrost”. From Finland to Ireland, they suddenly began heating up , many reaching 50C and food worth millions of euros had to be thrown away. But no actual hand was needed to cause the meltdown. This was a cyber-attack, or rather a chain of attacks. Like pretty much everything else in 2026, supermarket freezers are digitally enabled. That makes them smarter and more efficient, but like everything else that is connected to the internet, it also makes them more vulnerable. Russian hacktivists claimed they were behind some of the supermarket sabotage, but no one knows for sure. It could also be Iran, Iranian proxies, North Korea – or unaffiliated bedroom hackers. When Transport for London suffered a devastating hack two years ago, the culprits turned out to be two British teenagers . items.summary: Iran warns missile response to new attack could extend to Europe An Iranian lawmaker has warned that any new US or Israeli attack could prompt missile strikes reaching Europe, adding that the response could push oil prices above $150 a barrel. “The range of the responding missiles will also encompass Europe, and this will lead to the oil price crossing the $150 threshold,” Hosseinali Haji Deligani, a member of parliament, told Iran’s Tasnim news agency. He said Iran’s response would be “massive, multiplied and strategic”, without geographical limits. Haji Deligani also described the US naval blockade of Iran as “a form of war”, warning that Iranian forces would attack “at the appropriate moment”. On Tuesday, Iran’s top military commander warned that the country’s armed forces would respond to any threat without “geographical limits”.

items.summary: If foreign-policy restrainers of both parties are looking for a model the new Congress can follow once it takes office in January, they could do worse than to refer back to the 1974 midterm election that brought to Washington a tidal wave of young Democrats who quickly passed legislation placing unprecedented constraints on the power of the “Imperial Presidency,” which had reached its zenith under former President Richard Nixon. In many respects, the parallels between the 1974 midterms and the results of Tuesday’s election are eerie. Though Nixon, whose own imperial pretensions were more sartorial than architectural , had resigned from office three months before the vote, his abuses of executive powers loomed large over the election. Those abuses were, after all, hard to ignore: from Watergate and the impoundment of Congressional appropriations at home, to the secret bombing of Cambodia and Laos and the covert CIA campaign to overthrow the democratically-elected government of Chile abroad. items.summary: De tussentijdse verkiezingen in de Verenigde Staten hebben geleid tot een opvallende verschuiving van Republikeins rood naar Democratisch blauw. Republikeinen verloren de macht in staten waar zij decennia lang de senator leverden. Uit onvrede over het beleid van president Trump keerden velen hem de rug toe, is daarbij de uitleg. Wie zijn deze mensen? Uit voorlopige analyses blijkt dat kiezers van elke leeftijd, etniciteit, geslacht en opleidingsniveau van de Republikeinse partij naar de Democratische partij zijn overgestapt. De grootste veranderingen zijn te zien onder jonge kiezers, mannelijke kiezers, Latino-kiezers en mensen met de middelbare school als hoogste opleidingsniveau. Dat zijn allemaal groepen die twee jaar geleden, tijdens de presidentsverkiezingen, nog massaal op Trump stemden . items.summary: From energy prices to datacenters, climate became a cost-of-living issue – and a winning one Climate-forward Democrats swept into power on Tuesday night as a blue tsunami flipped the Senate, House and several governor’s races. Voters were laser-focused on affordability, and experts said Democrats succeeded in linking cost-of-living concerns with rising energy prices, datacenters and, to some extent, the climate crisis. They may have even created a path for a “new climate politics”. The results delivered a sharp rebuke of Donald Trump, who started a war with Iran that raised gas pump prices across the country and exposed the fragility of fossil fuels, all while the US oil industry earned $130bn in profits since the war began. Household energy costs soared, driven by various factors including constraints on renewables , climate disasters and a datacenter boom. Continue reading...

items.title: Tracking the blue wave: how our visual and data journalists helped you navigate the US midterm elections
items.summary: Ahead of the Democrats’ ‘Blue-nami’, some of the team behind our epic results page explained the work that goes into preparing for every election night On millions of screens around the world this week, the colour of the US electoral map digitally transposed. But behind the pixelated blue states and red states there were really 50 shades of purple. Some midterm races for the Senate and House of Representatives were closer than others. Some swings didn’t represent an actual shift in party allegiance. The shades and nuances in each race were always going to be important this year, with expectations that many Republican supporters wouldn’t turn out for their party because of specific issues, such as inflation, fuel prices, the Iran war, datacentres, or Donald Trump’s toxicity. items.summary: It has long been claimed that Americans do not vote based on foreign policy, but the results of Tuesday’s midterm elections demonstrated the limits of this truism, with a large majority of voters rejecting the Iran War waged by the Trump administration. Even before the election, an October Fox News poll indicated that the Iran war and issues associated with it (inflation and gas prices) were among the top issues voters were concerned about. Exit polling published by NBC News showed 74% of voters saw the Iran war as a “crucial” or “major factor” in their vote, while 62% believed using force against Iran was the wrong decision. This apparently has come as a nasty surprise to the war’s biggest defenders and surrogates, who had assured their followers that this backlash would not happen. Some have admitted their errors, but many have not, and that split has rapidly produced a circular firing squad, with neocons aggressively turning on those in their ranks who have conceded the war was a mistake. It named Indian nationals Suniel Kumar Sharma and his wife, Jaspreet Preeti Shahid, as well as two other Indian citizens who head two of the couple's businesses, and nine separate entities connected to Sharma. "Their schemes have provided false flags and certifications to sanctioned vessels involved in transporting Iranian petroleum, including vessels operating on behalf of the Iranian military and its proxies," the department said in a statement. items.summary: De Amerikaanse president Trump is flink afgestraft in de tussentijdse verkiezingen, de midterms. De Democraten krijgen door de blauwe tsunami nu zowel een meerderheid in het Huis als de Senaat. Wat betekent deze gigantische overwinning van de Democraten voor Donald Trump? Luister hier: Deze aflevering van De Dag luister je via NPO Luister en alle andere podcastapps. Bevalt het? Vergeet je dan niet te abonneren. Amerikakenner en jurist Kenneth Manusama legt in podcast De Dag uit wat de Democraten kunnen met die meerderheid. Want de wensen zijn duidelijk: Amerika moet betaalbaarder worden, de Iran-oorlog moet stoppen en de inzet van ICE-agenten moet veranderen. President Trump dreigde direct om z'n veto in te zetten, als het volgens hem de verkeerde kant op gaat. Maar Trump moet ook oppassen dat de Republikeinse partij wel achter hem blijft staan. Reageren? items.title: Usa, gli scanner respingono le schede elettorali: cosa è successo a New York
items.summary: Problemi agli scanner elettorali nella contea di Westchester, nello Stato di New York, durante le elezioni di Midterm. In numerosi seggi le macchine non sono riuscite a leggere le schede cartacee, restituendole agli elettori, come si vede nelle immagini girate a Yonkers. Per permettere la prosecuzione delle votazioni, i funzionari elettorali hanno disposto la raccolta delle schede in appositi sacchi di sicurezza, destinati al successivo conteggio. Secondo le autorità elettorali dello Stato, il problema è stato causato da un aggiornamento della programmazione degli scanner, che non erano in grado di riconoscere le schede utilizzate. Il responsabile dell'amministrazione della contea, Ken Jenkins, ha definito l'accaduto «completamente inaccettabile» e annunciato una verifica bipartisan per chiarire le cause del malfunzionamento. Le autorità hanno invitato i cittadini a continuare a votare, assicurando che tutte le schede valide sarebbero state conteggiate. Il guasto ha interessato anche i seggi di una circoscrizione contesa tra il repubblicano Mike Lawler e la democratica Cait Conley. ►

By midnight Democrats flipped six Senate seats — including in reliably red states like South Carolina, Texas, and Kansas. As of this morning, they added Michigan and Maine. In a rare inversion of historical trends, foreign policy played a serious role in the results of Tuesday’s midterm elections. The window is narrow, with one carrier due to return home after early November and moonless nights offering favourable conditions for attacks, the report said. clusters.headline: MAGA: Why Trump's most loyal supporters are turning against him?

items.title: MAGA: Why Trump's most loyal supporters are turning against him?
items.summary:
Is Trump losing the support of the very coalition that brought him back to power?
 
Just one day before the midterm elections, Trump's approval rating stands at 32%, one of the lowest ever recorded at this stage of a presidency.
 
And discontent is growing beyond Democratic voters. Some of Trump's most loyal Republican and MAGA supporters are increasingly torn between political loyalty and economic reality. The war in Iran, rising costs linked to the Strait of Hormuz blockade, unfulfilled “America First” promises and other controversial issues, including the Epstein files scandal, are widening the rift between Trump and his electoral base.
 
Can he regain control of the diverse coalition that makes up MAGA?
 
FRANCE 24 journalist Stella Elgersma spoke to MAGA and Republican experts to explore how the movement has evolved, what its supporters want and what is driving their discontent.
 
Watch the full youtube documentary : https://youtu.be/XkehRG77itY?si=iOfIl0PwrgyX-j0X

clusters.headline: Heading into the midterms, 'no US president in recent times has been as unpopular as Donald Trump'

items.title: Heading into the midterms, 'no US president in recent times has been as unpopular as Donald Trump'
items.summary: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Richard Johnson, Senior Lecturer in US Politics at Queen Mary University of London. He says that "Donald Trump is damaged goods at this point in his presidency." With this uncompromising assessment, Johnson takes us through the political forces shaping the 2026 US midterm elections. Far from assuming that Trump's formidable campaigning instincts can once again mobilize Republican voters, Johnson questions whether the president's political influence has become a liability for the very party he once transformed. He points to a potentially significant realignment within the American electorate. Economic grievances, rising living costs, trade disputes and disillusionment with the war in Iran appear, in Johnson's reading, to be weakening important elements of the coalition that sustained Trump's return to power. Particularly consequential is the possibility that Latino voters, agricultural communities and sections of the MAGA electorate may be reconsidering their political loyalties or withdrawing from electoral participation altogether.

items.title: Piraten kapen Iraans schip bij Somalië, mogelijk met meer aanvallen als doel
items.summary: Somalische piraten hebben een Iraans vissersschip aangevallen en overmeesterd. Er zijn 23 bemanningsleden aan boord van het schip. Dat meldt de EU-missie die moet bijdragen aan de veiligheid op de West-Indische Oceaan en de Rode Zee. Het schip werd donderdag gekaapt ten noordoosten van Somalië, tussen de kustplaatsen Bandar Bayla en Hafun. Volgens het veiligheidscentrum zijn de piraten gewapend en is onduidelijk hoe de bemanning het maakt. De EU-missie waarschuwt dat het schip mogelijk als uitvalsbasis wordt gebruikt voor meer piraterij. Het nadert een commerciële scheepvaartroute, volgens de laatst bekende positie. Twaalf piraten Een medewerker van de maritieme politie van Puntland zegt tegen persbureau AP dat er twaalf piraten aan boord zijn gegaan van het Iraanse schip, de Azini. Op het schip waren 21 Iraniërs en twee Somalische beveiligers. De EU-missie onderzoekt het incident. Schepen in de buurt zijn opgeroepen alert te zijn op verdachte situaties en die onmiddellijk te melden. Meer kapingen De afgelopen maanden zijn er nog vijf piratenaanvallen geweest voor de kust van Somalië

Small and medium unmanned aerial systems now provide persistent surveillance over dense urban terrain, support reconnaissance of subterranean infrastructure, accelerate the transfer of intelligence from sensors to commanders and strike platforms, and reduce the need to expose soldiers during the most dangerous stages of operations. Their integration with artificial intelligence, shared command-and-control networks, and increasingly autonomous systems has further shortened decision and response times. At the same time, the IDF’s growing reliance on drones has generated a continuing cycle of adaptation as adversaries employ electronic warfare, FPV drones, Fiber-optic control systems, and other countermeasures. items.summary: The proliferation of inexpensive FPV and attack drones is reshaping armored warfare and exposing vulnerabilities even in advanced platforms such as Israel’s Merkava Mk4M. Although the Trophy active protection system remains highly effective against conventional anti-tank threats, combat experience in Gaza, Lebanon, and Ukraine demonstrates the growing danger posed by steep-angle and top-attack drone strikes. Preserving the Merkava’s battlefield survivability will require a layered response combining purpose-built overhead protection, upgraded high-angle detection and interception capabilities, and vehicle-level electronic warfare. The challenge is not to replace Trophy, but to adapt Israel’s armored forces to a threat environment in which relatively cheap drones can impose disproportionate costs on even the most sophisticated tanks.

clusters.headline: The Iraqi Pipeline Game: How Cooperating with Iraq and Syria Can Help Israel Compete with Turkey

items.title: The Iraqi Pipeline Game: How Cooperating with Iraq and Syria Can Help Israel Compete with Turkey
items.summary: Recent wars involving Israel, the United States, and Iran altered the regional balance of power and severely disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. These developments increased the need for alternative overland oil and gas routes and intensified competition between Turkey and Israel as both seek to become important regional energy and trade corridors. Turkey has a geographic advantage, but it is not absolute. Iraqi and Syrian efforts to diversify their external dependencies present Israel with an opportunity to strengthen its regional leverage. If Israel acts while demand for alternative routes remains high, it could become an important transit hub for Middle Eastern oil bound for Europe.

clusters.headline: Israel and Lebanon: Analyzing Prospects for Peace

items.title: Israel and Lebanon: Analyzing Prospects for Peace
items.summary: Israel and Lebanon have technically been in a state of war since Israel’s founding in 1948, but recent diplomatic developments indicate that both the Israeli and Lebanese governments increasingly share an interest in cooperating to reduce Hezbollah’s influence and create an opportunity for lasting peace between the two countries. The June 2026 U.S.-backed 14-point framework agreement outlines a phased IDF withdrawal, LAF deployment, and the disarmament of Hezbollah as a path toward Israeli-Lebanese normalization. However, despite the progress, obstacles remain. Iran opposes Israeli-Lebanese normalization because it would weaken Hezbollah and consequently weaken Iran’s “Axis of Resistance.” Hezbollah rejects disarmament and warns that attempts by the LAF to force it could spark another civil war in Lebanon. To properly implement the 14-point framework agreement and move toward normalization, the LAF must strengthen its military capabilities so that it will be able to counter Hezbollah without further threatening internal stability. clusters.headline: EASTERN MEDITERRANEAN GAS CONSIDERATIONS

items.title: EASTERN MEDITERRANEAN GAS CONSIDERATIONS
items.summary: The Middle East has entered a period of sustained strategic instability in which conventional military conflict, proxy warfare, and competition over maritime chokepoints increasingly overlap. Iran has suffered significant military and economic pressure but can still impose costs through regional partners and by disrupting Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea shipping routes. At the same time, doubts about the reliability and limits of American security guarantees are shaping Gulf states' calculations. For Israel, the central strategic challenge is therefore shifting from achieving battlefield successes to translating military advantages into a more durable regional security architecture. This will require sustained cooperation with the United States and pragmatic Arab states while containing Iran and its remaining proxies and addressing the unresolved political and security questions surrounding Gaza.

clusters.headline: Syria: From Regime Preservation to Position Preservation

items.title: Syria: From Regime Preservation to Position Preservation
items.summary: Russia’s war in Ukraine has narrowed, rather than ended, Moscow’s role in the Middle East. Across Syria, Iran, and Gaza, Russia has shifted from costly power projection toward protecting existing assets, supporting partners without major new commitments, and maintaining diplomatic relevance at relatively low cost. Syria illustrates the clearest change: after once intervening to preserve the Assad regime, Moscow now focuses primarily on preserving its bases and regional access. Its restrained responses in Iran and limited influence in Gaza reveal the same pattern. Russia therefore remains an important regional actor, but the growing gap between its continued presence and its ability to shape outcomes reflects the priority Moscow now gives to the war in Ukraine.

clusters.headline: From the Battlefield to the Courtroom: Asymmetric Warfare, Lawfare and Israel’s War Against Hamas

items.title: From the Battlefield to the Courtroom: Asymmetric Warfare, Lawfare and Israel’s War Against Hamas
items.summary: The Israel–Hamas war demonstrates that modern asymmetric conflict is fought not only on the battlefield, but also in courts, international institutions, and the information environment. Hamas’s use of civilian areas, infrastructure, and indistinct combatant practices creates ambiguity that can be translated into legal and diplomatic pressure against Israel. While advanced targeting systems and artificial intelligence may improve military precision, they cannot by themselves resolve disputes over legitimacy, civilian casualties, or proportionality. Israel and other states confronting non-state actors must therefore integrate legal, diplomatic, and strategic communications planning into military operations from the outset, treating lawfare as a central component of contemporary warfare.

clusters.headline: The Western Label: Perceptions of Israel and Their Impact on International Diplomacy

items.title: The Western Label: Perceptions of Israel and Their Impact on International Diplomacy
items.summary: The article examines how the widespread perception of Israel as a “Western” state shapes international attitudes toward the country and its role in the Middle East. It argues that this characterization overlooks Israel’s deeply regional character, including its large Mizrahi, Sephardic, and Arab populations, and can distort the way Israeli conflicts and diplomatic relations are understood. At the same time, Israel has contributed to this perception through decades of political and cultural identification with the West. The article contends that developments such as the Abraham Accords demonstrate the potential benefits of viewing Israel as an integral Middle Eastern actor rather than as a Western outpost, and argues that a more accurate understanding of Israel’s regional identity could improve diplomacy and regional cooperation.

clusters.headline: Beyond the Missiles: Another Strategic Opportunity for Israel

items.title: Beyond the Missiles: Another Strategic Opportunity for Israel
items.summary: The India-Israel relationship has evolved from limited diplomatic engagement into a durable strategic partnership centered on defense cooperation. India’s post-Cold War diversification away from Russian arms created an opening for Israeli systems, while joint development, technology transfer, and India’s “Aatmanirbhar” defense policy have deepened bilateral military ties. Israel has consequently become a major supplier of missiles, air-defense systems, UAVs, and advanced military technology to India. The relationship also carries broader geopolitical significance. India’s strong ties with both Israel and Saudi Arabia, combined with its central role in the India-Middle East-Europe Corridor (IMEC), could give it an important role in facilitating deeper Israeli-Saudi economic cooperation and, potentially, future normalization. For Israel, therefore, ties with India provide not only defense revenues and strategic depth in Asia, but also a possible avenue for strengthening its position in the emerging Middle Eastern regional order and counterbalancing Iran.

clusters.headline: The U.S.-Israel Alliance is Stronger than Ever and More Divided than Ever

items.title: The U.S.-Israel Alliance is Stronger than Ever and More Divided than Ever
items.summary: The U.S.-Israel alliance remains exceptionally strong militarily but is becoming increasingly contested politically. Recent conflicts with Iran have produced unprecedented operational integration, including direct U.S. participation, missile defense support, intelligence sharing, and deeper coordination through CENTCOM, reinforcing Israel’s central role in U.S. regional defense policy. At the same time, strategic disagreements between President Trump and Prime Minister Netanyahu over Iran and Lebanon show that strong security support does not guarantee policy alignment. This divergence is increasingly reflected in American politics, where public opinion has grown more critical of Israel, Democratic lawmakers are more willing to challenge arms sales and military assistance, and even traditionally pro-Israel Democrats are distinguishing support for Israel from support for Netanyahu’s policies. clusters.headline: Power in Syria: Its Present, Future, and Israeli Interests

items.title: Power in Syria: Its Present, Future, and Israeli Interests
items.summary: Post-Assad Syria remains caught between promising state consolidation and persistent structural instability. Ahmed al-Sharaa’s Syrian Transitional Government (STG) has achieved notable diplomatic successes—including improved relations with Washington, Moscow, and the Gulf, sanctions relief, and resistance to renewed Iranian influence—but its domestic authority remains undermined by sectarian tensions, weak institutions, incomplete military integration, and the potential resurgence of ISIS. The Druze, Kurds, and Alawites continue to resist full centralization, while Turkey seeks to expand its influence and prevent Kurdish autonomy, creating a strategic challenge for Israel. Syria could therefore evolve toward consolidation, prolonged fragmentation, or renewed civil conflict, each requiring a different Israeli approach. Hegseth ligt onder vuur na de door de Republikeinen verloren tussentijdse verkiezingen van vorige week. Onder zijn leiding begonnen de Verenigde Staten een oorlog tegen Iran. items.title: Are Democrats ready to make the most of the blue wave?
items.summary: Unless you’ve been living under a rock (no shame Patrick Star!), you’ve likely heard about last Tuesday’s “Blue Wave” midterm elections . The Democrats’ strong performance at the polls flipped control of the House and the Senate, delivering stunning results on the way, including flipping long-time red states like Kansas and Texas. As the GOP scrambles to repair the damage and Democrats strategize about how to use their new power in a divided Washington, one takeaway seems obvious: this was a foreign policy election, in which the Iran war and the costs it brought home served as the tipping point. But can we read these election results as a repudiation of U.S. foreign policy writ-large, or is this a specific response to one of the dumbest interventions in the long history of American adventurism? What does JD Vance's day-after effort to distance himself from the war tell us about how Republicans are digesting this result? items.title: After midterm disaster, can Rubio still get Cuba regime change?
items.summary: After Democrats dominated last week’s midterm elections, retaking control of the House and Senate, President Donald Trump has turned his attention southward. “Cuba is falling. It’s a failing nation. It’s got an ideology very similar to what the Democrat ideology is,” he said Monday. “I would imagine it will fall fairly soon.” The comments suggest that, despite facing a stunning rebuke of his foreign-policy adventurism in Iran, Trump is not quite ready to give up on his goal, reiterated as recently as last month, of overthrowing the Cuban government. So is Trump poised to go beyond economic pressure and saber rattling by launching a military campaign against Cuba? The answer is “no” — or at least “not yet.” Many analysts predict that a lame-duck president constrained by domestic setbacks could seek redemption through foreign-policy achievements, including by lashing out at seemingly easier targets like an impoverished Caribbean nation. items.title: How water, energy, and climate are reshaping international security
items.summary: Water, energy, and mineral resources have long played a role in influencing and inciting political, ideological, and economic violence. But this violence is now worsening, driven by growing population pressures, expanding economies, and a fracturing and reforming of political alliances — and the wars in Ukraine, Israel-Palestine, and Iran. One surprising result may be an unanticipated acceleration of the global transition away from fossil fuels.

items.title: 'Junk history' and Swedish neutrality
items.summary: The historian Stephen Kotkin of Stanford’s Hoover Institution has penned an important new essay on the phenomenon of “junk history”: reductionist or plainly wrong interpretations of historical events that have little or no basis in empirical reality but are nevertheless “marshaled in policy debates as justification for action, up to launching wars.” The emblematic example, which has recently been used by advocates for the war with Iran, is the failure of British Prime Minister Neville Chamberlain to truly ensure “peace in our time” at Munich in 1938. As Kotkin once put it, “It turns out not everything is Munich. It turns out Munich wasn’t even Munich when you get down into the nitty-gritty details.” Another example of junk history is what many otherwise well-informed American observers think they know about Sweden’s conduct during World War II and the Cold War. items.summary: As part of an effort to keep Russia on the radar of African countries still struggling from some of the negative externalities of Russia’s continuing war in Ukraine, Russian President Vladimir Putin hosted African leaders in Moscow last week for the third Russia-Africa summit . Between October 28 and 29, Russian officials met with their African counterparts in high-level discussions covering a wide range of issues, primarily focused on continued security relations and opportunities for greater economic collaboration. Of course, Russian engagement with Africa isn’t new. The Russian paramilitary group Africa Corps has around 2,500 fighters on the continent, where it has formed relations with a number of African governments to fight armed groups in exchange for payment, including through access to commodities. items.title: A Fox Under a Pink Moon review – Iranian teen refugee paints boldly imaginative self-portrait
items.summary: Soraya Akhlaghi filmed her perilous flight from Iran and precarious new life over five years on her phone, reassembled here with yearning animations The world feels like an overwhelmingly forlorn place in this striking refugee self-portrait, shot on smartphone by Soraya Akhlaghi over five years and assembled remotely by co-director Mehrdad Oskouei. Fleeing a dead-end life as a Tehran maid, Soraya – who is just 16 at the beginning of the film – starts out at an Istanbul asylum centre. Most “games” – as border-crossing sorties with people-smugglers are euphemistically called – end in failure in the wilderness at the hands of hostile law enforcement officers. Soraya is hoping to join her mother, who left for Austria after the death of Soraya’s father when she was a child. She winds up back in the Iranian capital, with her violent husband. Corporate Re-entry as an Indicator of the End of the “Age of Wars”
items.summary: Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 marked not only a military but also an economic turning point in the international order. The mass withdrawal of multinational corporations (MNCs) from Russia demonstrated that geopolitical risk had begun to outweigh the benefits of global economic interdependence. But if corporate exit is one indicator of the beginning of a new “age of wars”, the gradual return of MNCs could be an indicator of its eventual end. Corporate return should not, however, be measured as a binary variable of returned/not returned. It is better understood as a sequence of increasingly costly and difficult-to-reverse commitments. This paper proposes a “corporate re-entry ladder” ranging from renewed institutional contacts and market reconnaissance to direct commercial presence and, ultimately, irreversible capital investment. The critical indicator of geopolitical normalization is therefore not the return of the first Western brand. items.title: Centcom sets up 'Task Force Iron Gate' to disrupt Iran’s weapons transfers
items.summary: Centcom sets up 'Task Force Iron Gate' to disrupt Iran’s weapons transfers The United States Central Command (Centcom) has directed the establishment of a task force that will support US government's efforts to prevent Iran from using ground routes to transport advanced weapons and other materials. In a statement issued on Saturday on X, Centcom said Admiral Brad Cooper has directed the formation of Task Force Iron Gate, an internal staff of approximately 20 civilian and military personnel based in Tampa, Florida. It will coordinate with other US government agencies on preventing the movement of advanced weapons systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials, and "illegal revenue streams" across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea, Centcom added. "The establishment of Task Force Iron Gate reinforces the success of our ironclad blockade against Iran at sea," said Cooper. "Strengthening CENTCOM's collaboration with U.S. inter-agency partners will further constrain Iran's ability to finance terrorism, rebuild weapons factories, and replenish their military." https://t.co/xUcO5

items.title: US military says it disabled cargo vessel in Gulf of Oman
items.summary: US military says it disabled cargo vessel in Gulf of Oman A US military aircraft fired on and disabled a commercial vessel that tried to break the US naval blockade of Iran on Saturday, US Central Command (Centcom) said. The St Kitts and Nevis-flagged cargo ship had visited an Iranian port and was trying to leave regional waters when a US plane fired precision munitions at its stern, after US forces ordered the crew to clear the targeted areas of the vessel, Centcom said. The US military also said on Saturday it was launching a task force to crack down on Iran’s movement of advanced weapons and other sanctioned material across its land borders and through the Caspian Sea, expanding on its months-long naval blockade. Centcom estimated that the blockade had prevented Iran from exporting more than $25bn worth of crude oil.

Explosions reported on Iran's Qeshm Island and in port of Jask
items.summary: Explosions reported on Iran's Qeshm Island and in port of Jask Explosions were heard on Saturday on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz and in the southern port of Jask, Iranian media reported, though there was no official confirmation of what caused them. The Iranian Tasnim news agency said earlier on Saturday that two missiles had struck Qeshm Island, but did not say who fired them. There was no official word on damage. The reported explosions come days after US strikes on the island, which a US official described as limited and not a resumption of major combat operations.

IRGC spokesman announces lifting of restrictions on Iranian missiles
items.summary: IRGC spokesman announces lifting of restrictions on Iranian missiles Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards has said that it has lifted restrictions on the range of Iran's missiles. IRGC spokesman, Brigadier General Hossein Mohebbi reportedly made the comments at a press conference on Saturday, in response to question regarding the country's supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei's warning to the US against further attacks on the country. Khamenei had previously said during a meeting with senior military commanders, that any renewed US or Israeli attck would be met with "with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response". The leader also reportedly ordered an update of Iran's military target database. According to Tasnim news agency, Mohebbi was asked on Saturday whether Khamenei's comments meant that limits on the range of Iranian missiles had been removed. He responded : "This restriction has been lifted for us". “Our duty is to show our capabilities on the battlefield,” he added.

items.summary: Journalist en oud-correspondent Thomas Loudon is overleden. Hij kampte met neuro-endocriene tumoren (NET), een langzaam groeiende vorm van kanker. Vorig jaar kreeg hij de diagnose en deze week overleed hij daaraan. Hij was 56 jaar. In 2001 werd Loudon de eerste Nederlandse (video)journalist die zich na de Islamitische Revolutie in Iran vestigde. Hij deed in diverse talen verslag van ontwikkelingen in Iran, Afghanistan en het noorden van Irak voor onder meer de NOS, Trouw en Elsevier, maar ook voor buitenlandse media als CNN, het Chileense Canal 13 en Asia TV in Singapore. Egypte en Jordanië In 2003 trok hij naar de Egyptische hoofdstad Caïro, waar hij Midden-Oostencorrespondent werd voor de NOS. Daarna deed hij dat vanuit Jordanië. Hij maakte onder meer verhalen over de Amerikaanse oorlog in Irak. Correspondent bleef hij tot begin 2007, waarna hij terugkeerde naar Nederland. In de jaren daarna was hij actief als docent journalistiek in Groningen en Rotterdam. items.summary: Acts of greyzone aggression aim to spread panic. Europe has to show the saboteurs that we are resilient It was as though a ghostly hand had switched the settings on supermarket freezers across Europe from “freeze” to “defrost”. From Finland to Ireland, they suddenly began heating up , many reaching 50C and food worth millions of euros had to be thrown away. But no actual hand was needed to cause the meltdown. This was a cyber-attack, or rather a chain of attacks. Like pretty much everything else in 2026, supermarket freezers are digitally enabled. That makes them smarter and more efficient, but like everything else that is connected to the internet, it also makes them more vulnerable. Russian hacktivists claimed they were behind some of the supermarket sabotage, but no one knows for sure. It could also be Iran, Iranian proxies, North Korea – or unaffiliated bedroom hackers. items.title: US and Iran edge closer to potential breakthrough in talks to end war, Bloomberg reports
items.summary: US and Iran edge closer to potential breakthrough in talks to end war, Bloomberg reports The United States and Iran are moving closer to a possible breakthrough in efforts to end the war, with Tehran considering proposals on its nuclear programme that it had previously been unwilling to discuss, Bloomberg reported, citing a diplomat familiar with the talks. The diplomat said Iran was studying proposals on its nuclear activities presented by Qatar, the main mediator. Any concession could help to advance negotiations, which have stalled since the collapse of an interim agreement reached in June. Reuters and The New York Times have also previously reported on Iran’s willingness to compromise on the nuclear issue. US President Donald Trump spoke by phone with Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani about efforts to de-escalate the conflict and secure a comprehensive agreement, the emir’s office said on Friday. Qatari officials have been shuttling between Doha and Tehran to help bridge differences, including over Iran’s nuclear activities and the US naval blockade of Iranian ports.

items.title: When the 'Watergate Babies' rode their own wave of anger
items.summary: If foreign-policy restrainers of both parties are looking for a model the new Congress can follow once it takes office in January, they could do worse than to refer back to the 1974 midterm election that brought to Washington a tidal wave of young Democrats who quickly passed legislation placing unprecedented constraints on the power of the “Imperial Presidency,” which had reached its zenith under former President Richard Nixon. In many respects, the parallels between the 1974 midterms and the results of Tuesday’s election are eerie. Though Nixon, whose own imperial pretensions were more sartorial than architectural , had resigned from office three months before the vote, his abuses of executive powers loomed large over the election. Those abuses were, after all, hard to ignore: from Watergate and the impoundment of Congressional appropriations at home, to the secret bombing of Cambodia and Laos and the covert CIA campaign to overthrow the democratically-elected government of Chile abroad. items.title: Aipac spent $55m on losing congressional candidates in midterm elections: Report
items.summary: Aipac spent $55m on losing congressional candidates in midterm elections: Report The American Israel Public Affairs Committee (Aipac) spent more than $84m in the 2026 US midterms, but nearly two-thirds of those funds were spent on losing candidates, according to a new report from Responsible Statecraft. Aipac’s Super Pac and other groups spent $55m on failed candidates. The largest portion of those funds, about $32m, was spent trying to defeat Democratic Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan. The results marked one of Aipac’s worst performances in years, suggesting that the US-Israeli war on Iran, which has contributed to soaring cost-of-living issues, resonated strongly with voters. In the 2022 midterms, Aipac’s Super Pac, United Democracy Project, saw 69 percent of its expenditure spent on races backed by the organisation that won. That number was even higher in 2024, after Israel’s genocide in Gaza, with 87 percent of its spending going to successful races. items.summary: The Democrats have gained new powers to constrain Donald Trump. But the drubbing that Republicans received could yet prompt him to new excesses Donald Trump is a president without parallel, but history can still be instructive. Lame duck presidents often focus on foreign policy to escape domestic discontent and establish a legacy in an area where a hostile Congress offers less of an obstacle. Mr Trump, who was stunningly rebuffed by voters in Tuesday’s midterms , might seek satisfaction in construction projects, the 2028 presidential race and his family’s future. Or, amid the humiliation and with Republican critics growing louder, he could distract attention with fresh adventurism – perhaps escalating against Cuba – or more likely a vengeful new offensive against Iran. Mr Trump won’t put in the legwork or attention to detail demanded by, say, Bill Clinton’s push for lasting peace in the Middle East. But lost in the conversation is that this was not just a rejection of the Iran war. It was also a repudiation of the broader foreign policy that repeatedly gets the U.S. into wars — or into supporting the wars and war crimes of U.S. partners. Trump famously ran on a promise to end forever wars and not to start new ones. items.title: Neocons in full meltdown as voters punish GOP for Iran war
items.summary: It has long been claimed that Americans do not vote based on foreign policy, but the results of Tuesday’s midterm elections demonstrated the limits of this truism, with a large majority of voters rejecting the Iran War waged by the Trump administration. Even before the election, an October Fox News poll indicated that the Iran war and issues associated with it (inflation and gas prices) were among the top issues voters were concerned about. Exit polling published by NBC News showed 74% of voters saw the Iran war as a “crucial” or “major factor” in their vote, while 62% believed using force against Iran was the wrong decision. This apparently has come as a nasty surprise to the war’s biggest defenders and surrogates, who had assured their followers that this backlash would not happen. Some have admitted their errors, but many have not, and that split has rapidly produced a circular firing squad, with neocons aggressively turning on those in their ranks who have conceded the war was a mistake. items.title: AIPAC dumped more than $55 million into losing midterm races
items.summary: The largest pro-Israel group in the U.S., the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC), has been silent on social media since Tuesday afternoon, well before polls closed across the country and Democrats won both chambers of Congress in a blue wave, largely driven by dissatisfaction over rising costs sparked by the war in Iran. The group was an early supporter of the war and a major funder of ads attacking House and Senate candidates calling to cut off aid to Israel. It spent big on the 2026 midterm elections, dumping $84.1 million via its super PAC, United Democracy Project (UDP), and several other PACs into races that have been decided as of this writing. AIPAC might be silent today because they need to explain to their donors how nearly-two-thirds, or $55.3 million, of that spending went to races in which the group’s preferred candidate lost. items.title: US issues fresh sanctions against individuals and entities aiding Iran
items.summary: US issues fresh sanctions against individuals and entities aiding Iran The US Treasury issued fresh sanctions on Wednesday targeting what it called "the vast criminal network" of companies and individuals tied to Iran. It named Indian nationals Suniel Kumar Sharma and his wife, Jaspreet Preeti Shahid, as well as two other Indian citizens who head two of the couple's businesses, and nine separate entities connected to Sharma. "Their schemes have provided false flags and certifications to sanctioned vessels involved in transporting Iranian petroleum, including vessels operating on behalf of the Iranian military and its proxies," the department said in a statement. The department also sanctioned Turkey-based Fugo Group Services Inc for its ongoing support of Iran's heavily sanctioned aviation sector.

items.title: Trump admits Iran war caused election losses but ‘we had to do it’
items.summary: Trump admits Iran war caused election losses but ‘we had to do it’ US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that the Iran war was responsible for his Republican Party's resounding midterm election defeat. Asked whether he agreed with Vice President JD Vance earlier remarks that the Iran war was "the reason we lost", Trump told reporters outside the White House ballroom construction site that his comments were "largely true because it drove the gasoline up a little bit short term". "But at the same time, if I had it to do again, I'd have to do it again. Because long term, it's the only answer. You can't let Iran have a nuclear weapon," he added. He also ruled out firing Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, saying "he's doing a very good job," despite his role in pushing for military action against Tehran. US President Donald Trump speaks to reporters before the construction site of the East Wing ballroom at the White House in Washington, DC, on 4 November 2026 (Mandel Ngan/AFP)

items.title: Podcast De Dag: de problemen van Trump
items.summary: De Amerikaanse president Trump is flink afgestraft in de tussentijdse verkiezingen, de midterms. De Democraten krijgen door de blauwe tsunami nu zowel een meerderheid in het Huis als de Senaat. Wat betekent deze gigantische overwinning van de Democraten voor Donald Trump? Luister hier: Deze aflevering van De Dag luister je via NPO Luister en alle andere podcastapps. Bevalt het? Vergeet je dan niet te abonneren. Amerikakenner en jurist Kenneth Manusama legt in podcast De Dag uit wat de Democraten kunnen met die meerderheid. Want de wensen zijn duidelijk: Amerika moet betaalbaarder worden, de Iran-oorlog moet stoppen en de inzet van ICE-agenten moet veranderen. President Trump dreigde direct om z'n veto in te zetten, als het volgens hem de verkeerde kant op gaat. Maar Trump moet ook oppassen dat de Republikeinse partij wel achter hem blijft staan. Reageren? Mail naar dedag@nos.nl Presentatie & montage: Marco Geijtenbeek Redactie: Rosanne Sies Eindredactie: Judith van de Hulsbeek

items.summary: Een blue wave is over Amerika gespoeld. De Democraten hebben zowel de meerderheid in de Senaat als het Huis van Afgevaardigden behaald. In januari worden de nieuwe leden beëdigd en de Democraten hebben grootse plannen om Trump in de laatste twee jaar van zijn presidentschap te dwarsbomen. Wat kunnen de Democraten eigenlijk doen als ze straks het Congres domineren? Eerst een stapje terug, want wat doet het Congres precies? Het Congres bestaat uit het Huis van Afgevaardigden en de Senaat. De 435 leden van het Huis stemmen over wetgeving, kunnen onderzoeken starten en documenten opvragen. Ook heeft het Huis de macht over de portemonnee. Alles wat uit de schatkist wordt gehaald, moet langs het Huis. Dan de Senaat, die bevestigt de benoeming van kabinetsleden, ambassadeurs en rechters, waaronder die van het Hooggerechtshof. Een meerderheid in de Senaat kan Trumps genomineerden blokkeren. items.title: Usa, gli scanner respingono le schede elettorali: cosa è successo a New York
items.summary: Problemi agli scanner elettorali nella contea di Westchester, nello Stato di New York, durante le elezioni di Midterm. In numerosi seggi le macchine non sono riuscite a leggere le schede cartacee, restituendole agli elettori, come si vede nelle immagini girate a Yonkers. Per permettere la prosecuzione delle votazioni, i funzionari elettorali hanno disposto la raccolta delle schede in appositi sacchi di sicurezza, destinati al successivo conteggio. Secondo le autorità elettorali dello Stato, il problema è stato causato da un aggiornamento della programmazione degli scanner, che non erano in grado di riconoscere le schede utilizzate. Il responsabile dell'amministrazione della contea, Ken Jenkins, ha definito l'accaduto «completamente inaccettabile» e annunciato una verifica bipartisan per chiarire le cause del malfunzionamento. Le autorità hanno invitato i cittadini a continuare a votare, assicurando che tutte le schede valide sarebbero state conteggiate. Il guasto ha interessato anche i seggi di una circoscrizione contesa tra il repubblicano Mike Lawler e la democratica Cait Conley. ►

items.title: Major losses could spur Trump to escalate war before year's end
items.summary: As much as the Iran war is the key reason Trump and the GOP were crushed tonight, it is important to recognize that the pressure for war is now likely to increase . This does not mean that Trump will restart the war. But the balance of pressure for and against war will likely favor escalation. Trump was under a degree of pressure to strike a deal before the midterms, hoping to soften the blow in the polls. But now that the midterms are over, that pressure will dissipate somewhat. Gas prices are still high, but the political cost has already been paid. There won’t be another point on the political calendar for some time when that cost can be exacted again. But two other factors will intensify. First, pro-war elements in Israel and in Washington will see the next two months as the last period in which Trump has wide maneuverability to restart the war. By January, the Democrats will control both chambers, will control the purse, and can begin impeaching Trump’s secretaries, including Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth. items.summary: Democrats secured an overwhelming victory in the midterm elections on Tuesday in a stunning rebuke to President Donald Trump’s first two years in office, winning majorities in both the Senate and House of Representatives. By midnight Democrats flipped six Senate seats — including in reliably red states like South Carolina, Texas, and Kansas. As of this morning, they added Michigan and Maine. In a rare inversion of historical trends, foreign policy played a serious role in the results of Tuesday’s midterm elections. Is Trump losing the support of the very coalition that brought him back to power?
 
Just one day before the midterm elections, Trump's approval rating stands at 32%, one of the lowest ever recorded at this stage of a presidency.
 
And discontent is growing beyond Democratic voters. Some of Trump's most loyal Republican and MAGA supporters are increasingly torn between political loyalty and economic reality. The war in Iran, rising costs linked to the Strait of Hormuz blockade, unfulfilled “America First” promises and other controversial issues, including the Epstein files scandal, are widening the rift between Trump and his electoral base.
 
Can he regain control of the diverse coalition that makes up MAGA?
 
FRANCE 24 journalist Stella Elgersma spoke to MAGA and Republican experts to explore how the movement has evolved, what its supporters want and what is driving their discontent.

items.title: Heading into the midterms, 'no US president in recent times has been as unpopular as Donald Trump'
items.summary: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Richard Johnson, Senior Lecturer in US Politics at Queen Mary University of London. He says that "Donald Trump is damaged goods at this point in his presidency." With this uncompromising assessment, Johnson takes us through the political forces shaping the 2026 US midterm elections. Far from assuming that Trump's formidable campaigning instincts can once again mobilize Republican voters, Johnson questions whether the president's political influence has become a liability for the very party he once transformed. He points to a potentially significant realignment within the American electorate. Economic grievances, rising living costs, trade disputes and disillusionment with the war in Iran appear, in Johnson's reading, to be weakening important elements of the coalition that sustained Trump's return to power. Particularly consequential is the possibility that Latino voters, agricultural communities and sections of the MAGA electorate may be reconsidering their political loyalties or withdrawing from electoral participation altogether.

items.title: Iran warns new war could last longer after Trump threatens strikes

Diplomatic efforts to end the Middle East war have been punctuated by repeated threats from the US and Israel to resume bombardments as they hold crucial elections. "A potential future war could last longer than previous conflict, and the American president would not be in a position to dictate the timing or the conditions of its conclusion," said army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia, according to Iranian state television. Akraminia's remarks followed Trump's suggestion that the US could swiftly strike its remaining targets in Iran.

items.title: Piraten kapen Iraans schip bij Somalië, mogelijk met meer aanvallen als doel
items.summary: Somalische piraten hebben een Iraans vissersschip aangevallen en overmeesterd. Er zijn 23 bemanningsleden aan boord van het schip. Dat meldt de EU-missie die moet bijdragen aan de veiligheid op de West-Indische Oceaan en de Rode Zee. Het schip werd donderdag gekaapt ten noordoosten van Somalië, tussen de kustplaatsen Bandar Bayla en Hafun. Volgens het veiligheidscentrum zijn de piraten gewapend en is onduidelijk hoe de bemanning het maakt. De EU-missie waarschuwt dat het schip mogelijk als uitvalsbasis wordt gebruikt voor meer piraterij. Het nadert een commerciële scheepvaartroute, volgens de laatst bekende positie. Twaalf piraten Een medewerker van de maritieme politie van Puntland zegt tegen persbureau AP dat er twaalf piraten aan boord zijn gegaan van het Iraanse schip, de Azini. Op het schip waren 21 Iraniërs en twee Somalische beveiligers. De EU-missie onderzoekt het incident. Schepen in de buurt zijn opgeroepen alert te zijn op verdachte situaties en die onmiddellijk te melden. Meer kapingen De afgelopen maanden zijn er nog vijf piratenaanvallen geweest voor de kust van Somalië

items.summary: Iran submits evidence of US-Israeli attacks on maritime infrastructure to IMO Iran said it has submitted evidence of US and Israeli attacks on its maritime infrastructure to the International Maritime Organisation (IMO). The dossier of evidence given by Tehran to the IMO includes documents and photographic evidence of sabotage on its maritime infrastructure. An Iranian official said IMO member states will discuss the evidence at a council session taking place in London on 2-6 November. The attacks on its maritime infrastructure, according to Iran, threaten the safety of international shipping and seafarers. Iran's IRNA news agency reported that damage to maritime traffic control systems also increases the risk of accidents, and the destruction of rescue facilities undermines emergency response capabilities.

items.title: How Tactical Drone Technology Has Strengthened IDF Effectiveness in Counterterrorism Operations
items.summary: The Israel Defense Forces’ rapid integration of tactical drones since October 7 has significantly improved operational effectiveness across three core areas: intelligence gathering, precision targeting, and force protection. Small and medium unmanned aerial systems now provide persistent surveillance over dense urban terrain, support reconnaissance of subterranean infrastructure, accelerate the transfer of intelligence from sensors to commanders and strike platforms, and reduce the need to expose soldiers during the most dangerous stages of operations. Their integration with artificial intelligence, shared command-and-control networks, and increasingly autonomous systems has further shortened decision and response times. At the same time, the IDF’s growing reliance on drones has generated a continuing cycle of adaptation as adversaries employ electronic warfare, FPV drones, Fiber-optic control systems, and other countermeasures. The resulting competition is driving Israel toward increasingly integrated reconnaissance, strike, electronic-warfare, and counter-drone capabilities. Tactic

items.title: A Chariot for Tomorrow’s War: Analyzing the Merkava Mk4M ‘Windbreaker’ in the Drone Age
items.summary: The proliferation of inexpensive FPV and attack drones is reshaping armored warfare and exposing vulnerabilities even in advanced platforms such as Israel’s Merkava Mk4M. Although the Trophy active protection system remains highly effective against conventional anti-tank threats, combat experience in Gaza, Lebanon, and Ukraine demonstrates the growing danger posed by steep-angle and top-attack drone strikes. Preserving the Merkava’s battlefield survivability will require a layered response combining purpose-built overhead protection, upgraded high-angle detection and interception capabilities, and vehicle-level electronic warfare. The challenge is not to replace Trophy, but to adapt Israel’s armored forces to a threat environment in which relatively cheap drones can impose disproportionate costs on even the most sophisticated tanks.

items.title: The Iraqi Pipeline Game: How Cooperating with Iraq and Syria Can Help Israel Compete with Turkey
items.summary: Recent wars involving Israel, the United States, and Iran altered the regional balance of power and severely disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. These developments increased the need for alternative overland oil and gas routes and intensified competition between Turkey and Israel as both seek to become important regional energy and trade corridors. Turkey has a geographic advantage, but it is not absolute. Iraqi and Syrian efforts to diversify their external dependencies present Israel with an opportunity to strengthen its regional leverage. If Israel acts while demand for alternative routes remains high, it could become an important transit hub for Middle Eastern oil bound for Europe.

items.title: Israel and Lebanon: Analyzing Prospects for Peace
items.summary: Israel and Lebanon have technically been in a state of war since Israel’s founding in 1948, but recent diplomatic developments indicate that both the Israeli and Lebanese governments increasingly share an interest in cooperating to reduce Hezbollah’s influence and create an opportunity for lasting peace between the two countries. The June 2026 U.S.-backed 14-point framework agreement outlines a phased IDF withdrawal, LAF deployment, and the disarmament of Hezbollah as a path toward Israeli-Lebanese normalization. However, despite the progress, obstacles remain. Iran opposes Israeli-Lebanese normalization because it would weaken Hezbollah and consequently weaken Iran’s “Axis of Resistance.” Hezbollah rejects disarmament and warns that attempts by the LAF to force it could spark another civil war in Lebanon. To properly implement the 14-point framework agreement and move toward normalization, the LAF must strengthen its military capabilities so that it will be able to counter Hezbollah without further threatening internal stability.
